To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bovine follicle is fully grown at preovulatory stage and oocyte maturation starts at the same stage.

1) in the preovulatory bovine follicle, oocytes are arrested at prophase I, 2) the first meiotic division of bovine follicular oocytes begins at the preovulatory stage, 3) the second meiotic division begins in the ovulated bovine oocyte, and 4) the second polar body is extruded in the bovine oviduct.

1) the oocytes in the antral follicle of the bovine ovary are arrested in prophase I of the first meiotic division, 2) the oocytes resume meiosis and enter the metaphase I stage at the time of the pre-ovulatory surge of luteinizing hormone, and 3) the oocytes enter the metaphase II stage at the time the follicle reaches a diameter of 12 mm.

the oocyte in the bovine ovary is in the prophase I of meiosis at the time of ovulation, and it is in the metaphase I at the time of fertilization, and in the telophase I at the birth of the calf.
in the bovine ovary, meiosis is initiated only after ovulation, and that the oocytes which are in the prophase of the first meiotic division at this time are the only ones that can complete meiosis.

the oocyte in a bovine ovarian follicle of about 12mm or greater in diameter, at the onset of estrus, is at the metaphase I stage of the first maturation division, and that it is the oocyte in the small follicles, 10mm or less in diameter, that is at the prophase I stage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the bovine oocytes in the antral follicles of 10 mm or more in diameter begin to enter into meiotic division at the time of ovulation, while the oocytes of 10 mm in diameter or less are arrested in prophase I even after the time of ovualtion.

the oocytes of bovine ovary are arrested in the prophase I of the first maturation division until the onset of estrus and that only oocytes of follicles of 10mm or more in diameter begin the first meiotic division and reach the metaphase I at the onset of estrous.

the development and maturation of oocytes is a very complex process that requires the coordination of many different cellular processes.
